## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13805: Glob search timeout — prevent infinite hangs (SMALL ~2-3h)

- **What**: Stalled glob operations (circular symlinks, permission errors on large directories, infinite recursion from malformed patterns) previously hung indefinitely, blocking the agent. Add configurable timeout (default 30s, overrideable via workspace/user config) to glob searches. When timeout expires, return partial results + log warning instead of hanging forever.
- **Why**: Pathological filesystems (circular symlinks in node_modules, permission errors on /proc or /sys when workspace root misconfigured, infinite recursion) lock up the glob tool indefinitely, requiring manual kill. Bounded timeout prevents agent lockups and provides partial results for most real searches (30s is enough for 100k+ files on SSD).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13805 (fix(cli): time out stalled glob searches)
- **Category**: tool
- **Size**: SMALL (~2-3h — Alexi has `src/tool/tools/glob.ts` using fast-glob. Wrap fast-glob stream in AbortController + timeout, return partial results on timeout, log warning. Add `globTimeout` config field to routing-config or tool config. Test with circular symlink fixture + permission-denied directory. ~80 lines tool change + 40 lines test.)

#### 2. Cline #13835: apply_patch Add File guard — prevent silent overwrites (SMALL ~1-2h)

- **What**: apply_patch tool has "File already exists" guard to prevent ADD operations from overwriting existing files (security + data loss prevention), but loadFiles only pre-loaded UPDATE/DELETE targets before parsing. The parser's "already exists" check never saw ADD targets, so fs.writeFile silently replaced existing files when an ADD patch targeted an existing path. Fix: load ADD targets in loadFiles too (read from filesystem if exists) so the guard fires correctly.
- **Why**: Silent overwrites violate the ADD semantic (create new file, fail if exists) and can cause data loss when patch intent is misclassified (e.g. AI hallucinates ADD for an UPDATE). Guard must see real filesystem state to work.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13835 (fix(core): make apply_patch Add File refuse to overwrite existing files)
- **Category**: tool
- **Size**: SMALL (~1-2h — Alexi has `src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts`. Audit loadFiles / pre-load logic: ensure ADD targets are read from filesystem before parsing (if file exists, load content; if not, skip). Verify "File already exists" guard fires for ADD operations targeting existing paths. Add test: apply ADD patch to existing file, expect rejection. ~30 lines change + 20 lines test.)

#### 3. Cline #13854: SearchCombobox section header preservation — grouped search UX (LOW priority, DEFER ~2-3h)

- **What**: ClinePass model provider lists the same model in both Subscribed tier and Free tier (e.g. cline-pass/deepseek-v4-flash in Subscribed, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash in Free), so when user searches "deepseek v4 flash", flattening the tier sections produced two identical-looking rows with no indication they were from different tiers. Fix: keep section headers visible during search for whichever sections still have matches, so duplicate model names remain distinguishable.
- **Why**: Duplicate model names across tiers are indistinguishable in flat search results, confusing users about which tier's quota they're consuming. Section headers provide the necessary context.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13854 (ui: keep section headers visible while searching in SearchCombobox)
- **Category**: command (TUI component)
- **Size**: LOW priority, DEFER (~2-3h — Alexi has no TUI SearchCombobox yet. Interactive mode (`src/cli/interactive.ts`) uses ink-select-input for simple flat lists (model selection, session selection), not grouped/sectioned lists with search-within-sections. This pattern is useful when Alexi adds grouped selection UI (e.g. models grouped by provider tier, tools grouped by category). Keep on radar for future TUI work. Implementation: render section headers conditionally when section.items.some(item => matchesSearch(item)); preserve section structure in filtered results instead of flattening. ~60 lines component change + 30 lines test.)

#### 4. Kilocode #13802: Marketplace publishing retry — transient failure handling (LOW priority, CI-infra-specific)

- **What**: VS Code extension publishing to Marketplace (vsce publish) and Open VSX (ovsx publish) occasionally fails with transient network errors or "version already exists" conflicts. Wrap publication in retry loop with 30s and 60s backoff, and skip duplicate upload errors independently per marketplace (so Open VSX 409 doesn't block Marketplace retry).
- **Why**: Transient failures break CI release jobs, requiring manual retry. Independent error handling per marketplace prevents one marketplace's state from blocking the other's publication.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13802 (fix(vscode): retry marketplace publishing)
- **Category**: ci
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no VS Code extension, no Marketplace publishing, no Open VSX registration. This is CI-infra-specific retry logic for extension distribution. Not applicable to CLI-first npm-published tool. (Alexi does have npm publish in release workflow, which already has retry logic via `npm publish --retry 3 --retry-timeout 60000`.)

#### 5. Kilocode #13796 + #13795: Indexing status sync + hidden polling removal — race-hardened state management (LOW priority, VS Code-extension-specific)

- **What**: VS Code extension's indexing status (consent UI, progress indicator) had race conditions: (1) hidden webview polling continued in background, wasting CPU; (2) indexing consent could be lost during visibility state transitions; (3) failed probes were not retried, leaving status stale; (4) diff file counts recalculated on every poll instead of reused. Fixes: (1) stop polling when webview hidden, restart on visible; (2) preserve consent across status races via explicit state guards; (3) retry failed probes and recheck sampled files; (4) reuse diff file counts from previous poll.
- **Why**: Hidden polling wasted CPU (10-20% on large repos), race conditions lost user consent (forcing re-prompt), failed probes made status stale until manual refresh, redundant diff calculations slowed polls.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13796, https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13795 (fix(vscode): keep indexing status in sync, fix(vscode): stop hidden polling and reuse diff file counts)
- **Category**: command (VS Code extension lifecycle)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no VS Code extension, no webview, no indexing status UI, no file-diff polling. This is VS Code-extension-specific state management. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 6. Kilocode #13764: JetBrains Ctrl+1/2/3/0 shortcuts — keyboard-driven mode/model cycling (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: Add keyboard shortcuts to JetBrains plugin: Ctrl+1 cycles mode (chat/architect/code), Ctrl+2 cycles model (within current provider), Ctrl+3 cycles reasoning effort (low/medium/high), Ctrl+0 resets to defaults. Shortcuts work in chat input, editor, and tool window.
- **Why**: Mouse-driven dropdowns slow down power users. Keyboard shortcuts enable rapid iteration (change model, retry prompt, cycle mode, all without leaving keyboard).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13764 (feat(jetbrains): add Ctrl+1/2/3/0 shortcuts to cycle mode, model, and reasoning effort)
- **Category**: command (IDE plugin UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no IDE integration, no mode/model/effort dropdowns. This is desktop-IDE-specific keyboard shortcut registration. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture. (Alexi CLI does support mode/model selection via `--mode`, `--model`, `--effort` flags and interactive prompts, which is the CLI-native equivalent.)
